mainTopic: Whether a fetus that died inside its mother carries נבלה טומאה, and the sources for which carcasses are טמא.
overview: The משנה deals with a shepherd who reaches into an animal's womb and touches a fetus that died there. The תנא קמא says he stays טהור whether the mother is kosher or not. רבי יוסי הגלילי says he is טמא if the mother is non-kosher. The גמרא explains the תנא קמא with רב חסדא's קל וחומר for a kosher mother, plus a היקש that extends the rule to a non-kosher mother. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבי יצחק reads 'paw-walkers among the animals' as 'paw-walkers inside a living animal,' and the גמרא tests this reading against cases like a cow inside a camel and a pig inside a pig. Because of the pig case, רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a new source: ויקרא 5:2 mentions only a non-kosher carcass, so it must mean a fetus, which follows its mother. Finally, a ברייתא shows רבי יונתן and בן עזאי searching for a source that a kosher wild animal's carcass is טמא. רבי יונתן rejects בן עזאי's source and gives רבי ישמעאל's: חיה and בהמה are included in each other, kosher with kosher and non-kosher with non-kosher.

steps.title: The case of the dead fetus and the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: A shepherd touches a fetus that died inside its mother. The תנא קמא rules he stays טהור, whether the mother is kosher or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal's fetus died inside its womb, and the shepherd reached his hand in and touched it. Whether the animal is non-kosher or kosher, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents a case: a shepherd touches a dead fetus while it is still inside its mother. The first opinion says he does not become טמא in either kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, touching a dead animal (נבלה) makes a person טמא. Here the תנא קמא says a dead fetus still inside its mother does not count as נבלה. This holds even when the mother is a non-kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure; here, the shepherd does not become impure

steps.confusionAlert: Here טהור and טמא are about טומאה from touching a dead animal. They are not about whether the fetus may be eaten. The words בהמה טמאה and בהמה טהורה do mean non-kosher and kosher animals.

phrases.english: MISHNA
An animal whose fetus died inside its womb

phrases.aramaic: וְהוֹשִׁיט הָרוֹעֶה אֶת יָדוֹ וְנָגַע בּוֹ,
phrases.english: and the shepherd reached in his hand and touched it,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בֵּין בִּבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה –
phrases.english: whether in a non-kosher animal or in a kosher animal –
he is pure.
phrases.notes: The fetus does not count as a נבלה, so the shepherd who touched it stays pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁמֵּת עוּבָּרָהּ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעֶיהָ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead fetus touched inside its mother's womb does not make a person טמא, whether the mother is kosher or non-kosher.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי splits between kosher and non-kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees. He holds the shepherd becomes טמא if the mother is non-kosher, but stays טהור if she is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: in a non-kosher animal it is impure, and in a kosher animal it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה draws a line between the two kinds of animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees with the תנא קמא about a kosher mother. He disagrees only about a non-kosher mother, where he says the dead fetus does carry נבלה טומאה. The גמרא will now look for the source of each side.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on a kosher mother (טהור). The argument is only about a non-kosher mother.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
in a non-kosher animal – it is impure,
and in a kosher animal – it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the תנא קמא in the case of a non-kosher mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal makes a person טמא; inside a kosher animal it does not.

steps.title: What is the first opinion's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the תנא קמא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא holds that the dead fetus is טהור. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead animal is usually a נבלה, so the תנא קמא needs a reason why this fetus is different. The גמרא wants a source, not just the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic behind the תנא קמא's ruling that the dead fetus is טהור.

steps.title: רב חסדא's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא argues: if the mother's שחיטה can permit the fetus to be eaten, it can surely also keep the fetus from being נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is a קל וחומר. If its mother helps to permit it for eating, should she not help to purify it from the impurity of a carcass?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers with a קל וחומר, a logical argument from a bigger case to a smaller one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus found inside a kosher animal that was slaughtered may be eaten without its own שחיטה; the mother's שחיטה covers it. Permitting food is the bigger thing, so the mother's power should surely be enough to keep the fetus from counting as נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if the harder case is true, the easier case is surely true
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; it carries טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: This argument only works for a kosher mother. A non-kosher mother never permits anything for eating, which is why the next step asks about her.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is a kal vachomer:
if its mother is effective
to permit it for eating,
phrases.notes: He means that slaughtering the mother makes the fetus inside her permitted to eat.

phrases.english: should she not be effective for it
to purify it from the impurity of a carcass?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the תנא קמא's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: the mother's power to permit the fetus for eating should also keep it from being נבלה.

steps.title: What about a non-kosher mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the קל וחומר only covers a kosher animal and asks for a source for a non-kosher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found this for a kosher animal; from where do we know it for a non-kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in רב חסדא's answer and sets up the next step to fill it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal's slaughter never permits eating, so the קל וחומר has no starting point there. Yet the תנא קמא rules טהור even for a non-kosher mother, so another source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found a source for a kosher animal;
for a non-kosher animal, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that רב חסדא's קל וחומר only covers part of the תנא קמא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal is also טהור.

steps.title: A פסוק links non-kosher animals to kosher ones
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק mentions both kinds of animals together, creating a היקש. So the non-kosher fetus is treated like the kosher one: טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And when an animal dies": this is a non-kosher animal. "Of those that you eat": this is a kosher animal. Non-kosher is compared to kosher. Just as a kosher animal's fetus is pure, so too a non-kosher animal's fetus is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that puts both kinds of animals side by side. That lets the kosher rule carry over to the non-kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's first words, "when an animal dies," are read as non-kosher animals. The next words, "of those that you eat," are kosher animals. Because the תורה joins them in one פסוק about נבלה, they share the same rules. So the kosher rule from the קל וחומר applies to non-kosher animals too.

keyTerms.meaning: A derivation from two things placed together in one פסוק, so they share rules

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא uses two steps: a קל וחומר for a kosher mother, then a היקש to stretch it to a non-kosher mother.

phrases.english: The verse states:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: "And when an animal dies" –
this is a non-kosher animal;
"of those that are yours to eat" –
this is a kosher animal.
A non-kosher animal is compared to a kosher animal:
just as with a kosher animal, its fetus is pure,
so too with a non-kosher animal, its fetus is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a non-kosher mother by bringing a היקש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש from ויקרא 11:39 compares non-kosher animals to kosher animals, so the fetus is טהור in both.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the other opinion and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks why רבי יוסי הגלילי says a non-kosher mother's fetus is טמא. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא just showed a היקש making both animals the same. So רבי יוסי הגלילי needs a source that singles out the non-kosher fetus as טמא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנא קמא's sources to the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that a fetus inside a non-kosher animal is טמא.

steps.title: רבי יצחק reads the פסוק about animals that walk on paws
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads a פסוק about non-kosher paw-walking animals as meaning "those inside a living animal I made impure for you." So a dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The verse says, "And whatever walks on its paws, among all the animals that walk": those that walk on paws inside a living animal, I made impure for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's source by reading a פסוק about non-kosher animals in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק says paw-walking animals are טמא. רבי יצחק reads בכל as "inside" and חיה as "a living animal," so the פסוק is about a dead paw-walker found inside a living animal: a fetus. The next steps work out which mothers this covers, so that a non-kosher mother's fetus is טמא and a kosher mother's is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Its paws; animals without split hooves, which are non-kosher
Usually a wild animal; here read as "a living animal"

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one word in a פסוק can be read differently. Reading בכל as "inside" is what gives רבי יוסי הגלילי his split between kosher and non-kosher animals.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Because the verse states:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:27

phrases.english: "And whatever walks on its paws
among all the animals that walk, etc." –
those that walk on paws inside a living animal
phrases.notes: He reads בכל as "inside" and חיה as "living animal", so it means a fetus inside a live animal.

phrases.english: I have made impure for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּאָמַר קְרָא וְכׇל הוֹלֵךְ עַל כַּפָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי יוסי הגלילי's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 11:27, read as "paw-walkers inside a living animal are טמא," makes a dead fetus inside a non-kosher animal טמא.

steps.title: A fused-hoof fetus inside a cow should be impure
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק makes paw-walking fetuses inside an animal טמא, then a קלוט fetus inside a kosher cow should be טמא too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, a fused-hoof fetus inside a cow should be impure, since it is a paw-walker inside an animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's reading of the פסוק. It points to a case where his reading seems to give the wrong result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קלוט has round, unsplit hooves, so it looks like a 'paw-walker.' If the פסוק simply means 'a paw-walker inside an animal is טמא,' then a קלוט inside a kosher cow would be טמא. But a fetus of a kosher cow should be טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces a challenge from the last idea)
An animal whose hooves are not split, round like a horse's
Animals that walk on paws (unsplit feet)

phrases.english: If that is so,
a fused-hoof fetus inside a cow should be impure,
since it is a paw-walker inside an animal?
phrases.notes: This is borrowing the words of ויקרא 11:27, as רבי יצחק read them in step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the פסוק given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's reading of 'paw-walkers inside an animal' as a rule about fetuses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, the rule would make a קלוט fetus of a kosher cow טמא, which cannot be right.

steps.title: The פסוק means four-walker inside four-walker; a cow walks on eight
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only speaks of a paw-walker inside a mother that also walks on four; a cow, with split hooves, walks on eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק means a paw-walker inside a four-walker. But this is a four-walker inside an eight-walker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק more exactly: the mother must also be a 'four-walker.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the animal 'walks on four.' A cow's split hooves give it eight parts touching the ground, so it is not a 'four-walker.' So a קלוט inside a cow is outside the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that walk on four (four whole, unsplit feet)
Animals that walk on eight (four split hooves = eight parts)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Eight' does not mean eight legs. A split hoof counts as two parts, so four split hooves make eight.

phrases.english: The פסוק means paw-walkers inside four-walkers,
phrases.notes: From the end of ויקרא 11:27: 'that walks on four.'

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי מְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע בִּמְהַלְּכֵי שְׁמֹנֶה הוּא.
phrases.english: but this is a four-walker inside an eight-walker.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְהַלְּכֵי כַפַּיִם בִּמְהַלְּכֵי אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any paw-walker inside any animal is טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a paw-walker inside a mother that walks on four is covered; a cow walks on eight.

steps.title: Then a cow fetus inside a camel should not be impure
steps.stepSummary: With the narrower reading, a cow fetus (eight-walker) inside a camel (four-walker) would not be covered, so it would not be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a cow fetus inside a camel should not be impure, since it is an eight-walker inside a four-walker!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new narrow reading. Now the problem is that the rule seems too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A camel is non-kosher, so its dead fetus should be טמא. But if the fetus is shaped like a cow, it walks on eight, not on paws. So the narrow reading would leave it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Cow (a kosher animal with split hooves)
Should not make impure / not be impure

phrases.english: Then a cow fetus inside a camel should not be impure,
since it is an eight-walker inside a four-walker,

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרָה בִּמְעֵי גָמָל לֹא תְּטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrow reading given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only a paw-walker inside a four-walker is covered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A cow-shaped fetus of a non-kosher camel should be טמא, but the narrow rule leaves it out.

steps.title: The extra word 'וכל' includes a cow inside a camel
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'וכל הולך' instead of just 'הולך'; the extra word brings in a cow fetus inside a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could have said 'walks'; it says 'and whatever walks,' to include a cow inside a camel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to an extra word in the פסוק that widens the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'הולך.' Adding 'וכל' ('and whatever') teaches that more cases are included. So a cow fetus in a camel is טמא even though it is not a paw-walker.

keyTerms.meaning: And whatever (an extra word that widens the rule)

phrases.english: It could say 'walks'; it says 'and whatever walks' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:27. The גמרא is pointing out that the word 'וכל' is extra.

phrases.english: to include a cow fetus inside a camel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלֵךְ, וְכׇל הוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק that includes more cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A cow-shaped fetus in a camel is outside the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'וכל' includes it, so it is טמא.

steps.title: Then a fused-hoof fetus inside a fused-hoof mother should be impure
steps.stepSummary: A קלוט fetus inside a קלוטה kosher mother is a four-walker inside a four-walker, so the פסוק would make it טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then a fused-hoof fetus inside a fused-hoof mother should be impure, since it is a four-walker inside a four-walker!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another case. Here the narrow reading seems to make a kosher animal's fetus טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a kosher mother that has unsplit hooves, a קלוטה, carrying a קלוט fetus. Both walk on four, so the פסוק fits exactly. But since the mother is kosher, its fetus should be טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A female animal with unsplit hooves (here, a kosher one)

phrases.english: Then a fused-hoof fetus inside a fused-hoof mother should be impure,
phrases.notes: The mother is a kosher animal, like a cow, that was itself born with unsplit hooves.

phrases.english: since it is a four-walker inside a four-walker!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָלוּט בִּמְעֵי קְלוּטָה לִיטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge to the 'four inside four' reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'four-walker inside four-walker' reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This case fits the פסוק exactly, yet the fetus of a kosher mother should be טהור.

steps.title: That is exactly what רב חסדא's קל וחומר is for
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's קל וחומר covers every kosher mother, so it keeps this case טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is exactly where רב חסדא's קל וחומר does its job.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this case is already handled by the קל וחומר from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא argued that the שחיטה of a kosher mother keeps her fetus from being נבלה. That reasoning works for any kosher mother, even one with unsplit hooves. So the קל וחומר overrides the פסוק here.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule has three parts. A paw-walking fetus inside a mother that walks on four is טמא through the פסוק. A cow inside a camel is included by 'וכל.' Any kosher mother keeps her fetus טהור through רב חסדא's קל וחומר.

phrases.aramaic: לְהָכִי אַהֲנִי קַל וָחוֹמֶר דְּרַב חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: For this, the קל וחומר of רב חסדא is useful.
phrases.notes: This is the argument from step 4: the mother's שחיטה keeps the fetus from being נבלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהָכִי אַהֲנִי קַל וָחוֹמֶר דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by bringing back רב חסדא's קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different source covers the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק makes a קלוט inside a קלוטה טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא's קל וחומר keeps every kosher mother's fetus טהור.

steps.title: רב אחדבוי בר אמי: then a pig inside a pig would not be impure
steps.stepSummary: A pig has split hooves, so a pig fetus in a pig is eight inside eight, outside the פסוק, yet it should be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי objected: then a pig inside a pig should not be impure, since it is an eight-walker inside an eight-walker!
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב אחדבוי בר אמי, attacks the 'four inside four' reading. The next step answers it by bringing a new source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pig is non-kosher, but it has split hooves like a cow. So a pig fetus inside a mother pig is neither a paw-walker nor inside a four-walker. The narrow reading would leave out a case that clearly should be טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it (a strong challenge from an אמורא)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami objected to it:
Then a pig fetus inside a female pig should not be impure,
since it is an eight-walker inside an eight-walker!
phrases.notes: A pig has split hooves, so it counts as walking on eight, just like a cow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fresh challenge to the 'four inside four' reading after the earlier challenges were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the פסוק only covers a four-walker inside a four-walker.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A pig inside a pig is eight inside eight. Neither the פסוק nor 'וכל' (which only added a cow in a camel) seems to cover it, yet it must be טמא.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Since the earlier source ran into the pig problem, רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a new source: the פסוק about one who touches a carcass of a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we learn it from here: 'A person who touches anything טמא, or the carcass of a non-kosher wild animal, or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal, or the carcass of a טמא creeping creature.'
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא tells us the גמרא is dropping the earlier way of learning the rule. רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes a new פסוק, and the next step will explain how it teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading depended on how many legs the fetus and mother walk on, and a pig fetus inside a pig broke that rule. This new פסוק says nothing about legs. It only talks about the carcass of a 'טמאה' (non-kosher) animal, and that word will be the key.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from this source
The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה
A small creeping creature, like a mouse or lizard

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: from here:
"A person who touches anything impure,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2

phrases.english: or the carcass of a non-kosher wild animal,
or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal,
or the carcass of an impure creeping creature."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that the pig question in step 15 knocked out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the source with a new פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule came from 'וכל הולך על כפיו', which depends on legs and fails for a pig.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from ויקרא 5:2, which depends only on whether the mother is kosher.

steps.title: Why the פסוק must be talking about a fetus
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'carcass of a non-kosher animal', but a kosher animal's carcass is also טמא. So the פסוק must mean a fetus, which is טמא inside a non-kosher mother and טהור inside a kosher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only the carcass of a non-kosher animal that makes things טמא, and a kosher one does not? Rather, what is this talking about? It is a fetus: inside a non-kosher animal it is טמא, and inside a kosher animal it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the פסוק. The word 'non-kosher' looks unnecessary, so it must be teaching something new about a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a kosher animal's נבלה is also טמא, so the פסוק cannot mean only non-kosher animals are טמא. It must be pointing to a case where kosher versus non-kosher really matters: a fetus. Since the test is the mother's kind, the pig fetus is now easily טמא, because its mother is non-kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus, an unborn animal still inside its mother
Is it really so that...? (a question showing something cannot be right)
Which one is this? What case is the פסוק talking about?

steps.whatToRemember: A fetus follows its mother: inside a non-kosher mother it is טמא, inside a kosher mother it is טהור, no matter how it walks.

phrases.english: Does the carcass of a non-kosher animal impart impurity,
and that of a kosher one does not impart impurity?
Rather, which one is this?
This is a fetus, which inside a non-kosher animal is impure,
and inside a kosher animal is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מְטַמְּאָה, וּבִטְהוֹרָה לֹא מְטַמְּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 16 proves the rule.
steps.raayaObject: A fetus is טמא inside a non-kosher mother and טהור inside a kosher mother.

steps.title: Why do we still need רבי יצחק's source?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule comes from רב נחמן בר יצחק's פסוק, why did רבי יצחק need his own source?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the rule comes from רב נחמן בר יצחק's source, why do I need רבי יצחק's source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need two sources for the same rule. The next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק learned the rule from 'וכל הולך על כפיו'. If ויקרא 5:2 already teaches it, his source seems unneeded. The גמרא assumes each source must teach something, so it looks for a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is already learned from...

phrases.english: And since it is derived
from the statement of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak,
why do I need that of Rabbi Yitzchak?
phrases.notes: Rabbi Yitzchak's source is 'וכל הולך על כפיו', the פסוק discussed in the earlier steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that a second source exists, asks why the first is still needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra thing does רבי יצחק's source add?

steps.title: Without רבי יצחק, we would use the פסוק only for רבי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: Without רבי יצחק's source, we would have thought ויקרא 5:2 is used fully for a teaching of רבי, so רבי יצחק shows the fetus rule is also learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for רבי יצחק, I would have said the whole פסוק comes to teach what רבי learns from it. So רבי יצחק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רבי יצחק's source is needed so we will know ויקרא 5:2 also teaches the fetus rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי learns a different teaching from this same פסוק. Without רבי יצחק, we might think the פסוק is completely used up by רבי's teaching and has nothing left for the fetus. רבי יצחק's source tells us the fetus rule is real, so we can read it in the פסוק too.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (what we might have wrongly thought)

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: If not for Rabbi Yitzchak, I would have said:
the whole verse comes for what Rabbi teaches,
phrases.notes: רבי is רבי יהודה הנשיא; the גמרא brings his teaching from this פסוק later.

phrases.english: so he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק's source is needed so we know ויקרא 5:2 is not used up only for רבי's teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא's habit of making sure every source has a job, even when two sources seem to teach the same thing.

steps.title: רבי יונתן begins listing which carcasses are טמא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יונתן told בן עזאי what we already know: a carcass of a kosher domesticated animal, a non-kosher domesticated animal, and a non-kosher wild animal all make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן said: I said to בן עזאי: we learned that the carcass of a kosher domesticated animal makes things טמא, and the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal makes things טמא, and the carcass of a non-kosher wild animal makes things טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא. רבי יונתן is setting up a list of what we already know, so he can next ask about a case that is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three of the four kinds of carcasses are already covered by פסוקים. Look at what is left off the list: a kosher wild animal. The next step asks about it.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yonatan said:
I said to ben Azzai:
We learned that a carcass of a kosher domesticated animal imparts impurity,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: and that a carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal imparts impurity,
phrases.notes: This one and the next come from ויקרא 5:2, the פסוק quoted above.

phrases.english: and that a carcass of a non-kosher wild animal imparts impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: נַמְתִּי לוֹ לְבֶן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about which kinds of נבלה are טמא, touching on the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carcasses of a kosher domesticated animal, a non-kosher domesticated animal, and a non-kosher wild animal are all טמא, each learned from a פסוק.

steps.title: What about a kosher wild animal's carcass?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן points out the missing case: from where do we know that a kosher wild animal's carcass is טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have not yet learned about the carcass of a kosher wild animal. Where do we learn that it makes things טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן names the one case still missing from the list in the last step. This question sets up the search for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 covered three kinds of animal: kosher בהמה, non-kosher בהמה and non-kosher חיה. The fourth kind, a kosher חיה, has no source yet. The rest of the ברייתא looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה
A kosher wild (undomesticated) animal, like a deer

phrases.english: The carcass of a kosher wild animal
we have not learned; from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He means: from where do we know it makes things טמא, like the three cases in the last step.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִבְלַת חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה לֹא לָמַדְנוּ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the fourth case missing from the list in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the carcass of a kosher חיה is טמא.

steps.title: בן עזאי's source: 'among all the wild animals'
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי suggests the פסוק 'whatever walks on its paws, among all the wild animals' as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to me: the source is the פסוק 'Whatever walks on its paws, among all the wild animals that walk.'
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי answers that the kosher חיה is learned from ויקרא 11:27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי reads the wide wording 'בכל החיה' (among ALL the wild animals) as including every חיה, even a kosher one. So in his view a kosher חיה's carcass is also טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Said (a rare word, used here instead of אמר)
Walks on its paws, like a cat or a dog

phrases.english: He said to me:
phrases.notes: Here בן עזאי is the one speaking to רבי יונתן.

phrases.english: "Whatever walks on its paws
among all the wild animals that walk."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:27

steps.triggerLanguage: נָם לִי: כָּל הוֹלֵךְ עַל כַּפָּיו בְּכׇל הַחַיָּה הַהֹלֶכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'בכל החיה' in ויקרא 11:27 include a kosher חיה.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: that verse is about a fetus
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן rejects the proof. The פסוק says 'among' the wild animals, so it is about a fetus inside a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Does the פסוק say 'and every wild animal'? It only says 'among all the wild animals.' It comes to teach about paw-walkers found inside a wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן challenges בן עזאי. He argues the פסוק is already used for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah meant every חיה, it would have said 'וכל חיה' (and every wild animal). The word 'ב' (among, inside) points to an animal that is inside a חיה, meaning a fetus. So the פסוק teaches about a fetus, not about a kosher חיה's carcass.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יונתן is not saying a kosher חיה is טהור. He only says this פסוק is not the source for it, because it is already used for the fetus.

phrases.english: I said to him:
But does it say "and every wild animal"?
Doesn't it say only "among all the wild animals"?
It comes to teach about paw-walkers inside a wild animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַמְתִּי לוֹ: וְכִי נֶאֱמַר וְכׇל חַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source offered in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's reading of 'בכל החיה' in ויקרא 11:27
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'ב' means 'inside', so the פסוק is about a fetus. It cannot also teach that every חיה, kosher ones included, is טמא.

steps.title: בן עזאי asks for רבי ישמעאל's view
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי asks what רבי ישמעאל, רבי יונתן's teacher, says about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: And what does ישמעאל say about this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that his source was rejected, בן עזאי asks רבי יונתן for his teacher's source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question moves from בן עזאי's own source to רבי ישמעאל's. The goal is still to find where a kosher חיה's carcass is shown to be טמא.

phrases.english: He said to me:
And what does ישמעאל say
phrases.notes: This is רבי ישמעאל, רבי יונתן's teacher.

phrases.english: about this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָם לִי: וּמָה יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר בְּדָבָר הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rejection in step 23, asks for a different source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי ישמעאל's source for the kosher חיה's carcass being טמא.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's source: 'when a domesticated animal dies'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן brings רבי ישמעאל's reading of ויקרא 11:39. The פסוק covers both kosher and non-kosher בהמה, and חיה is included in בהמה and the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: 'And when a domesticated animal dies' means a non-kosher animal. 'Of those that you eat' means a kosher animal. And we learned that חיה is included in בהמה, and בהמה is included in חיה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן gives רבי ישמעאל's source. He reads two parts of one פסוק and adds a general rule that חיה and בהמה include each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק teaches a non-kosher בהמה, and the second half teaches a kosher בהמה. Since the word בהמה also covers חיה, a kosher חיה is included too. That fills the missing case.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in (part of the same category)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that חיה and בהמה can include each other is a tool used in other places to apply a law written for one to the other.

phrases.english: I said to him:
"And when a domesticated animal dies":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: this is a non-kosher animal;
"of those that you eat":
this is a kosher animal.
We have learned that a wild animal is included in 'domesticated animal',
and a domesticated animal is included in 'wild animal'.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַמְתִּי לוֹ: וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה זוֹ בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 11:39 covers kosher and non-kosher בהמה, and since חיה is included in בהמה, a kosher חיה is covered too.

steps.title: Matching kosher with kosher, non-kosher with non-kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן adds detail: a kosher חיה is grouped with a kosher בהמה, and a non-kosher חיה with a non-kosher בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kosher wild animal is included with a kosher domesticated animal, and a non-kosher wild animal is included with a non-kosher domesticated animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן continues his answer and explains exactly how the inclusion works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inclusion goes kind with kind. When the Torah says kosher בהמה, it also means kosher חיה, and the same for non-kosher. So 'of those that you eat' covers the kosher חיה, which is the case we were missing.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל learns the kosher חיה from ויקרא 11:39, because a kosher חיה is included in 'kosher בהמה'. בן עזאי's source was rejected because that פסוק is used for a fetus.

phrases.english: A kosher wild animal is included in a kosher domesticated animal,
a non-kosher wild animal is included in a non-kosher domesticated animal,

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּה טְהוֹרָה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the inclusion rule of step 25 works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kosher חיה goes with kosher בהמה, and non-kosher חיה with non-kosher בהמה, so the kosher חיה is covered by 'of those that you eat'.
